scope: Course schedule, submission snapshots, final report, and teacher-reviewed workflow innovation bonus. This policy does not change leaderboard cells, weights, eligibility gates, or dynamic performance references.

day_1.name: kickoff_and_baseline
requirements: Start the service and pass public protocol checks.

day_3.name: first_candidate
requirements: Implement and validate the first end-to-end candidate.

day_4.name: midterm_snapshot
submission: A full immutable PR commit SHA available to the teacher before the cutoff.
A public evaluator artifact generated from that SHA.
A concise midterm summary naming the baseline, candidate, target cells, results, and known limitations.
day_4.late_change_policy: Changes after the cutoff belong to the final snapshot and are not included in the midterm cohort.

steps: Freeze the submitted cohort by full PR SHA.
Build every entry from a clean checkout on the same RTX 4090 environment.
Run the required vLLM control, public and hidden suites, and cohort scorer.
Publish a named midterm leaderboard snapshot and concise feedback.
midterm_teacher_action.publication_timing: After the unified evaluation completes; do not publish rolling scores from partial cohorts.

day_5.name: leaderboard_analysis
requirements: Interpret the midterm snapshot and teacher feedback.
Select the bounded final optimization hypothesis.

day_6.name: final_candidate_and_report
requirements: Complete final correctness and performance validation.
Prepare reproducibility artifacts and the detailed final report.

day_7.name: final_submission
submission: Detailed REPORT.md in the PR; an exported PDF is optional.
Canonical submission, efficiency output, raw evidence references, and reproduction commands.

eligibility: The submission passes the public functional suite.
The workflow does not weaken correctness, timing, hardware, model, or fallback contracts.
The final report contains reproducible evidence for the workflow claim.
examples: Reproducible baseline/candidate orchestration that reduces manual error.
Artifact provenance, hashing, comparison, or failure-triage automation.
Reusable shape/tactic search or profiler workflow tied to end-to-end validation.
Automated capacity-boundary probing and recovery verification.
A public/hidden-safe experiment workflow that improves evidence quality.
not_sufficient: A cosmetic command wrapper without measured value.
Hard-coded public cases, expected outputs, or benchmark-specific shortcuts.
A workflow that changes the frozen workload or hides fallback.
An unmeasured novelty claim without reusable artifacts or tests.
workflow_innovation_bonus.award_policy: The bonus rewards validated experimental workflow innovation. It cannot make an ineligible leaderboard submission eligible and cannot make the final course grade exceed 100.

final_report.suggested_length: Equivalent to 6-10 pages of technical content; prioritize evidence over padding.
required_sections: Frozen deployment, model, hardware, workload, and timing contract.
Correctness, reliability, performance, VRAM, MFU/BWU, and optional profiler evidence.
Accepted, rejected, negative, and inconclusive experiments.
Midterm-to-final changes and interpretation of leaderboard feedback.
Known limitations, unsupported modes, and rollback plan.
Exact build, serve, evaluator, and reproduction commands.
Conclusion and one bounded next step.
required_references: Public submission artifact and raw evidence hash.
compute_efficiency.py output or an explanation of unavailable fields.
Profiler capture IDs when profiler-derived claims are made.
final_report.grading_note: A report is evaluated for evidence quality, causal reasoning, reproducibility, negative-result handling, and alignment with the submitted implementation.
